# Fixes, before and after

Each example is a golden fixture under `tests/fixtures`, and the tests hold every one to the code.
The findings are what the gate reports today, and each after is exactly what `--fix` writes.
[RULES.md](../../RULES.md) has one short example per rule, and this page has the longer cases.

## Reported, then rewritten

A paragraph over its budget has no fixer, because where it breaks depends on its topics.
Its finding names the sentences to break after, and a rewrite that follows it changes no word.
A list rule can settle a long paragraph first, as the last case shows.

### One topic

The gate reports, from [`one-topic`](https://github.com/jpeakai/jpai-prose-gates/tree/main/tests/fixtures/paragraph/one-topic):

```text
before.md:1 paragraph-sentence-budget-exceeded paragraph has 7 sentences (budget 5) and one topic throughout; break it after sentence 4, where neighbouring sentences share the fewest words
```

Before:

```text
The fix engine applies every verified edit in a fixed rule order.
Each edit names the rule that proposed it and the expectation it claims.
The engine reparses the document after each edit and compares the trees.
A tree that changed shape sends the edit back as a refusal.
The engine keeps looping until no rule proposes a verifiable edit.
That loop ends at stable text, which the engine writes once.
A second fix run over stable text proposes no edit at all.
```

Rewritten by hand from the finding, with no word changed:

```text
The fix engine applies every verified edit in a fixed rule order.
Each edit names the rule that proposed it and the expectation it claims.
The engine reparses the document after each edit and compares the trees.
A tree that changed shape sends the edit back as a refusal.

The engine keeps looping until no rule proposes a verifiable edit.
That loop ends at stable text, which the engine writes once.
A second fix run over stable text proposes no edit at all.
```

### Semicolon list

The gate reports, from [`semicolon-list`](https://github.com/jpeakai/jpai-prose-gates/tree/main/tests/fixtures/paragraph/semicolon-list):

```text
before.md:1 list-semicolon-delimited-run semicolon-delimited list (3 ';'); promote to a bullet list
```

Before:

```text
A release runs from the Publish workflow on main.
The workflow needs: a version bump; a changelog entry; a green build; and a signed tag.
It then uploads the package to npm.
The tag starts the GitHub release.
The release notes come from the merged pull requests.
Nothing in that path runs from a laptop.
```

After `--fix`:

```text
A release runs from the Publish workflow on main.
The workflow needs:

- a version bump
- a changelog entry
- a green build
- a signed tag

It then uploads the package to npm.
The tag starts the GitHub release.
The release notes come from the merged pull requests.
Nothing in that path runs from a laptop.
```

### Topic shifts

The gate reports, from [`topic-shifts`](https://github.com/jpeakai/jpai-prose-gates/tree/main/tests/fixtures/paragraph/topic-shifts):

```text
before.md:1 paragraph-sentence-budget-exceeded paragraph has 7 sentences (budget 5) and about 3 topics; break it after sentences 3 and 6, one topic per paragraph
```

Before:

```text
The parser reads each markdown file once.
It builds a syntax tree that every rule shares.
Parsing twice would let two rules disagree about the tree.
Releases publish from GitHub Actions on main.
A release needs a signed tag and a green build.
The publish workflow refuses to run from a branch.
Plugins load on their own from the project folder.
```

Rewritten by hand from the finding, with no word changed:

```text
The parser reads each markdown file once.
It builds a syntax tree that every rule shares.
Parsing twice would let two rules disagree about the tree.

Releases publish from GitHub Actions on main.
A release needs a signed tag and a green build.
The publish workflow refuses to run from a branch.

Plugins load on their own from the project folder.
```
